summary: Amy Sims Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees from Wesleyan University (BA, 1989) and the University of Virginia (MA, 1995; PhD, 2004), studying under doctoral supervisor David Germano and several traditional and academic teachers.
Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed as a professor at the University of Washington around 1995.

Ana Agud is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Salamanca (~1966–1974) and the University of Tübingen (~1972–1976), later serving as a professor at the University of Salamanca around 1989.

Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. Educated at Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, St. Benedict's, S. Thomas' College, and Royal College, Colombo, he founded the Maha Bodhi Society (1891) and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Freiburg, Naples, and Cagliari, and taught at Visva-Bharati, Patna, Allahabad, Lucknow, and BHU, while serving as Ācārya of Arya Maitreya Mandala.

Anagarika Munindra (1915–2003) was a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner and teacher. He studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka, and served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.

Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology teacher who studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche. He held a teaching post at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Anand A. Yang is a historian and Indologist who studied at Swarthmore College (~1966–1970) and the University of Virginia (~1970–1976). He held posts at the University of Utah (1975), Sweet Briar College (~1975–1976), and the University of Washington (~2002).

Anand Venkatkrishnan is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Columbia University in 2015. He was appointed Assistant Professor of the History of Religion in South Asia at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Ananda Guruge (1928–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Ceylon and University of London. He held posts at NIEPA (attested 1970), CSU Fullerton, and the University of the West (attested 2012).

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy (1877–1947) was a scholar in Indology, art history, and philosophy who studied at Wycliffe College and University College London. He directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon and held curatorial and research posts at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar (1898–1959) was an Indologist and historian. He served as professor at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949) and Patna University (~1949–1957), chaired the Numismatic Society of India (1947), and directed the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

Anantalal Thakur (1916–2009) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta under several mentors. He served as professor at the Mithila Institute across several periods and directed the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of the West Indies, under Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds. He served as professor of religion at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).

Andrea Acri is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at Leiden University (~2006–2011) under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen. In 2016, he became an assistant professor in tantric studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University (PhD, 2010). She held faculty positions at IUPUI and Indiana University Bloomington, becoming a full professor in 2021.

Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who earned her degrees at the Free University of Berlin. As of 2026, she holds research posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the University of Munich.

Andreas Doctor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, in addition to studying under several traditional Rinpoches. He has held a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Andreas Spengel (1838–1905) was a scholar in linguistics and related fields. He completed his studies at the University of Munich (~1857–1860) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1860–1863), and he taught Albert Grünwedel.
Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams, while also studying under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
